I am 70 years old, farmed this land for 50 years. Only finished primary school. My farm is 4.1 mu, just me and my old woman working it. We grow winter wheat then summer maize, same as everyone in Quzhou. I don't read books about farming, I just do what I learned from my father and what I see working in the village.

For wheat, I sow improved seed, the kind they sell at the dealer, like Jimai. I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu when I sow in October — that's 50 kg. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread another 40 kg of urea per mu. My neighbor Old Wang did this last year and his wheat looked good. I know fertilizer is expensive now, but losing yield is worse than wasting a bit of fertilizer. I irrigate three times: once before winter to keep the seedlings alive, once at jointing when it gets warm, and once when the grains are filling. I spray pesticide twice — herbicide in spring, then once for bugs. I use the rotary tiller before sowing wheat. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu, hope for the same this year.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer has. After wheat harvest in early June, there is no time to plough, so I hire the no-tillage seeder to sow directly. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then 30 kg of urea when the corn is at the big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice if the sky doesn't give rain. Two sprays: one for weeds, one for corn borer. Maize usually gives about 520 kg per mu, sometimes more if the weather helps.

I don't try new things. My land is small, only 4 mu, so every yuan matters. But I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than have my family go short on grain.
